εἰς δὲ γῆν τῶν ἀπορφανισάντων ἑαυτοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ, κτῆμα δὲ δαιμόνων τὴν
κακίαν ἔχοντας, μὴ εἰσέλθῃς, δι' ἣν ἐστερήθησαν τοῦ ἐπουρανίου Πατρός· ὁ γὰρ
λυτρού μενος αὐτοὺς Κύριος ἐκ τοῦ ὑπερλάμπρου φωτὸς ἀπὸ σκότους, ἰσχυρός ἐστιν.
Υἱὸς ὀρθὸς ἐνδιατρίψει τὰ χείλη αὐτοῦ σοφίᾳ, καὶ ἡ σοφία πρὸς αὐτὸν συλλαλήσει
καὶ διαμενεῖ· ὁ δὲ στρεβλὸς ἐκπεσεῖται ἀπ' αὐτῆς. Εἰ τῷ φόβῳ Κυρίου ἐκκλίνει τις
ἀπὸ κακοῦ, καλῶς παραινεῖ διὰ πάσης τῆς ζωῆς ἐκκλίνειν ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ παντὸς κακοῦ.
Πᾶς ὁ ἐν κακίᾳ μέθυσος, καὶ ὁ ἐκ σοφίας πρὸς ἀγνωσίαν καταπορνεύων, πτωχεύσει
ἐκ θείας χάριτος· καὶ οὐκ ἐνδύσεται ἔνδυμα τοῦ γάμου πᾶς ὁ ἐν τῇ δαι μονιώδει
νυκτὶ ὑπνώδης, ἀλλὰ τὴν ὡς ῥάκος τετραυ ματισμένην σάρκα διαθλίβων γεέννης
φλόγα. Ἔφη τις τῶν γερόντων, τὴν ψυχὴν εἶναι μητέρα τοῦ νοῦ, ψυχὴν λέγων τὸ
παθητικὸν τῆς ψυχῆς, θυμόν τε καὶ ἐπιθυμίαν· διὰ γὰρ τῶν πρακτικῶν ἀρετῶν εἰς
φῶς προάγει τὸν νοῦν· διὰ γὰρ ἀνδρείας καὶ σω
pass_a_gloss: Avoid the land of those who have made themselves fatherless from God, treating evil as demonic property, having lost the heavenly Father; the Lord who rescues them from dazzling light out of darkness is strong. A upright son will weigh his words with wisdom, and wisdom will converse with him and stay; the perverse will drop from it. If someone shuns evil out of reverence for the Lord, he properly advises us always to flee all evil. Anyone sunk in vice, and the one who from wisdom falls into ignorance, will be poor before God’s favor, and will not wear the bridal robe—each who in the demon-haunted night is half-asleep will not cloth himself but will beat his flesh like torn cloth with hell’s fire. An elder taught: the soul mothers the intellect, meaning the soul’s passive faculty—anger and longing—for through active virtues he lifts the mind to light; by bravery and moderation we gain wisdom and divine knowledge, which are strengths of anger and longing; he may even call the mother the old Covenant, not to be scorned. On earth, about instructors, he remarks on their works: but those who composed and taught them, and who shaped the path to heaven, he named rovers; for many have taught, yet they did not fashion their road to heaven, since they neglected it; for he who speaks while walking—meaning who acts and instructs—walks suitably of the vocation he received from God. Sin in thought is like a bowl; sin in action is like a cup. The overreaching part is the pestle used by cooks: it strikes much but does not open what it hits. The Lord tells His disciples: Knock, and it will be opened. A mind accepting foreign ideas dwells on evil thoughts; the one who guards himself inherits life. Insensitivity to pain is dreadful. You will say, when struck in conscience, that you did not seek rewards of old age nor escape torments; they mocked me—17.225, meaning they insulted me—but I, wanting not to know when the soul’s dawn comes nor when sin is recognized. The house of virtues, built with divine wisdom, is constructed and made upright by understanding, fear of God, and knowledge. The one concerned with faith or any shipwrecked virtue is an unskilled pilot in battle against opposing forces in theology and virtue; but the one who sails with skill seems to have on earth the mind that anticipates God’s help, a counseling heart, the heart that does all things with counsel. This can be said of every virtue: there is shipwreck in temperance, love, greed, and every doctrine, as happens similarly to the catholic and apostolic Church. But if, with skill in warfare, one must fight opponents, then our life on earth is like a naval battle; for if we wish, we overwhelm them in heartfelt prayer and reason directed toward God, composed and ordered. If we refuse to resist, we are carried away; if we fight them, even if their war is strong, it means nothing; we defend ourselves only by fasting and self-restraint, and we destroy them and their arms like a spider breaking its web; if we also listen to the Lord’s voice where two or three are—heart, mind, soul—they unite in His presence, and the Lord is with us; all God does when we understand, and all He teaches when we act, never breaks His word; wisdom’s gates are action and mind’s contemplation, by which God’s wisdom enters; they turn neither right nor left, judging good and evil in assembly; they imitate good, draw near evil; those unwilling to learn God’s wisdom and knowledge face present death opposed by eternity; the fool is one made sweet in God’s wisdom, then left it, joined folly, and died with sins; if virtue lessens vice, vice is clearly destroyed by virtue; this happens in the coming age until vice ends; the defiled is destroyed, not corrupted; impurity is destroyed by practice or harsh punishment; we must apply this saying to those judged worthy of divine things.
pass_b_english:
Do not enter the land of those who have orphaned themselves from God, who hold wickedness as a possession of demons, from whom they were deprived of the heavenly Father; for the Lord who redeems them from the surpassingly brilliant light out of darkness is mighty. A righteous son will ponder his lips with wisdom, and wisdom will speak with him and remain with him; but the twisted one will fall away from her. If one turns away from evil by the fear of the Lord, he rightly urges us through all of life to turn away from every evil. Every person drunk in wickedness, and the one who from wisdom prostitutes himself into ignorance, will become impoverished from divine grace; and he will not put on the wedding garment—every one who in the demonic night is drowsy with sleep, but instead, wearing his flesh as a ragged and torn garment, he will torment himself with the fire of Gehenna. One of the elders said: the soul is the mother of the mind, speaking of the soul as the passive part of the soul—anger and desire—for through practical virtues he advances the mind into light; for by courage and self-control we acquire wisdom and knowledge of God, which are virtues of anger and desire; he might also say that the mother is the ancient Covenant, which is not to be despised. Here, concerning the teachers, he says of their writings: but those who made them and taught them, and who made the journey toward heaven, he called wanderers; for many have taught, but they did not make their journey toward heaven, because they did not guard it; for the one who converses in walks—that is, who acts and teaches—walks worthily of the calling to which he was called by God.

Sin is like a bowl when it exists only in thought, but when it is carried out in action, it becomes like a cup that holds the deed. The overreaching part, however, is what cooks call the pestle: it strikes many blows against the substance it hits, yet it does not open the place it strikes. To His disciples, the Lord says: Knock, and it shall be opened to you. A mind that receives a foreign thought or teaching will dwell on evil reasoning; but the one who guards himself will inherit life as an inheritance. How dreadful is insensitivity to pain! Then you will say, while being struck in the conscience, that you did not strive to attain the rewards of old age, nor to be freed from torments; they mocked me, 17.225—that is, they insulted me—but I, desiring not to know when the dawn of the soul comes, nor when the recognition of sin arrives. The house of virtues, built with divine wisdom, is constructed and, with understanding, the fear of God and knowledge, is set upright. The one concerning faith, or any of the virtues that are shipwrecked, is an unskilled pilot heading into battle against opposing forces, both in theology and in virtue; but the one who sails with skill in warfare seems to possess the mind on earth that anticipates God’s help, a counseling heart, the heart that does all things with counsel; and it is possible to say the same thing regarding every virtue: for there is also shipwreck concerning temperance, and concerning love, and concerning greed, and concerning every single doctrine, which likewise happens to the catholic and apostolic Church; but if, with skill in warfare, one must fight against the opponents, then our life upon the earth is like a naval battle; for if we wish, we overwhelm them in prayer of the heart and in reason directed toward God, composed and ordered.

If we do not wish to resist, we are swept away like those who drift upon the waters; and if we are also made to war against them, even if their war is great and fierce, it amounts to nothing; we shall fortify ourselves solely by fasting and self-control, and we shall cut them off and their weapons as a spider severs its web; and if we also hearken to the voice of the Lord, wherever two or three are gathered—heart, mind, and soul— they shall agree together in being contained within His bounds, and the Lord will be with us. For all that God does, when we understand it, and all that He teaches, when we put it into practice, in no way transgress His word; the gates of wisdom are the practical deeds, and the contemplation of the mind, through which the wisdom of God enters; they do not turn aside, neither to the right nor to the left, because they reckon themselves to be in councils discerning good and evil; and they counterfeit the good, while they approach the evil. To those who do not wish to be instructed by the wisdom and knowledge of God, through the present death the eternal stands opposed; the foolish one is he who has been sweetened in the wisdom of God, then forsaken it, and now joins himself to folly; therefore he also perished with his sins; but if virtue diminishes wickedness, then wickedness is clearly destroyed by virtue; and this will come to pass in the age to come, until wickedness ceases; for what is defiled will be, instead of corrupted, destroyed; and impurity is destroyed either by practice or by severe chastisement. It is necessary to use this saying toward those who have been deemed worthy of divine things.
